items.why: Letterboxed silhouette film: fog, lamp light and a slow camera carry a wordless story. The most cinematic piece in the library.
A photon's 170,000-year escape from the Sun told in 20 seconds, ending on a human eye and the line "YOU BLINKED." The best concept-to-payoff of the short pieces.
One character from birth to death. An age counter and heartbeat readout run throughout, and the art style changes with each life stage. Built to loop.
Cinematic Earth and Sun renders with running counters. A data poem with real pacing and restraint.
Five-minute film built around a gravitationally lensed black hole render. Slow and contemplative, with Chinese captions.

The same lesson retold as a corporate explainer, a terminal session, an 8-bit game, a nature documentary, film noir, kids' TV, an infomercial, a movie trailer and a bare HTML page. The widest stylistic range in the library.
Four-minute animated short with characters, a storm sequence and dialogue captions, held together by a consistent colour script.
Five-minute 3D cartoon episode: stylised characters, a moving camera and a bold purple, red and yellow palette.
Poster-grade graphic design with a new palette and type system for every chapter, Indic scripts set alongside Latin.
Real-time 3D shot like live action: sunset pier, lens flares, shallow depth of field, close-ups on the pedals and the beak.
One continuous aerial take with painterly clouds, sea reflections and a rolling camera.
A single unbroken scene that drifts from sunset to a moonlit night over water while lines of classical Chinese verse appear in vertical type.
98-second exploded-view 3D explainer with a clean studio-white look, from a one-line prompt. Its soundtrack is close to silent. The site also lists the same film and prompt under @mdaman010.
Shader-driven kaleidoscopic eye tunnel with iridescent liquid-metal forms. The most visually intense 20 seconds in the library.
A point becomes a line, a circle, a sphere, a lens, a ball, a flock and a world, laid out like numbered figures in a book. Concept and restraint over spectacle.
Swiss and Bauhaus poster typography that escapes its own layout grid: primary colours, huge type, 60fps.
Epicycles drawing pi, Lissajous curves, a Julia set, a phyllotaxis spiral and Euler's identity. The maths drives the motion.
Vertical ad built from classical engravings and serif type on white, cut fast. The creator attached a reference video (see the site's note).
items.note: using any reference with a fast edit (5s video is enough)

items.why: Risograph print look: halftone grain, misregistered pink, blue and yellow inks, Korean typography.
Lyric typography timed to an attached song, built on sun and eclipse imagery. Needs your own music track.
A particle murmuration that reshapes into network maps and a timeline in one flowing take. Data visualisation as choreography.
The widest technical range of the showreels: reflective 3D primitives, a fluid simulation, a particle vortex and sliced type.
One orange dot links every scene, bookended by a "Reduce Motion" toggle, with a halftone ripple and a 3D ring of type. A structured, reusable prompt.
A strict two-colour editorial system (ultramarine on cream) at 60fps. Made with the library's standard showreel prompt, which 28 entries share; this is the most disciplined result.
The same showreel prompt with the opposite result: lime glass and chrome 3D knots with heavy kinetic type, 32 seconds.
Apple-keynote style launch film in one continuous take. Scenes morph into each other and it ends on hands holding a framed print. Needs your photos, a song and a stock clip.
A single shape morphs through a button, a player, a slider, a toggle, tabs, a chart and a command palette, driven by a cursor.
A white ball bounces through sliders, notifications and a keyboard in one take, so every interface change lands as a physical impact.
Dark, minimal product film with a 3D carousel of vertical clips. Needs 10 to 20 clips you own.
Brand film in orange halftone and serif type: a dot-matrix upload, a globe, an infinity loop.
Polished dark SaaS launch film: a link being typed, a globe, live dashboards, a constellation of partners.
3D props (a big red button, slot reels, dice, a coin) cut against a light-trail vortex and glitch type.

Real talking-head footage cut out and dropped into eight visual styles (kawaii, manga, rubber-hose cartoon, holographic card, 8-bit and more) with synced captions. The only real-footage edit in the library.
